jobs.occupation: Position for a Postdoc (m/f/d) at the Chair of International Political Studies (Politologe/Politologin)
jobs.description: Position for a Postdoc (m/f/d) at the Chair of International Political StudiesUniverisity of Witten/HerdeckeWitten/Herdecke University (UW/H) is Germany’s first privately funded university. It was founded in 1982 and has since established itself as a leading educational institution in Germany. Today, the university employs more than 900 staff members, and a total of 3,700 students are enrolled in the Faculties of Health Sciences and of Economics and Social Sciences in Witten.Job descriptionThe team at the Chair of International Political Studies examines the causes and consequences of political violence. Its research focuses on questions regarding the relationship between conflict prevention strategies—such as power-sharing—and the risk of civil war in ethnically divided societies, as well as the impact of local political violence on voter preferences in OECD countries.To strengthen our team, we are seeking a PostDoc (m/f/d) to join the Chair of International Political Studies, starting April 1, 2027. The position (40h/ - 100%) is limited to 2 years.We are looking for an researcher who wants to develop their research agenda, which is not limited to the priorities of the research group. The position comes with a large amount of freedom to work on your own research priorities. We expect openness towards developing joint research projects that translate into funding applications. We offer participation in an active research network, the Conflict Research Exchange Workshop (CREW), international conference funding, and the possibility of remote work.Your tasksYou develop your own research profile in the field of international relations, historical political economy, or comparative politics, you support third party funding applications, and you teach one seminar per year (2 hours/week in one semester).Your profile- You have an an excellent doctoral degree in political science, economics, or related disciplines, or are about to complete your dissertation- You have an excellent command of English, strong knowledge of statistics, quantitative empirical social research, and causal research designs, as well as proficiency in R or Python- You showcase the ability to work both as part of a team and independently.- Relevant publications or experience in working in scientific projects are desirable.Wir bieten- Zusätzliche freie Brückentage- Vereinbarkeit von Beruf und Familie- Direkter Zugang zu medizinischer Versorgung- Verschiedene Bezuschussungen- Weiterbildung- Umweltfreundliche MobilitätsmöglichkeitenContactIf this opportunity aligns with your goals, please apply unit 24th November 2026, exclusively online, including the standard application documents (Resume without a photo, relevant transcripts, two academic papers or chapters from your doctoral dissertation, and contact information for two references) and your proposed start date.We look forward to receiving your application.Prof. Nils-Christian Bormann  | Professor of International Political Studies | nils.bormann@uni-wh.deConcept of diversityWe explicitly live and promote the idea of diversity (www.uni-wh.de/diversity (http://www.uni-wh.de/diversity) ). jobs.description: Ihre AufgabenThe University of Bonn is an international research university offering a broad range of subjects. With a 200-year history, some 31,500 students, more than 6,000 employees and an outstanding reputation in Germany and abroad, the University of Bonn is one of the leading universities in Germany and has been awarded the status of a University of Excellence.The Department of Southeastasia is looking to fill the following position from January 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible, initially on a fixed-term contract according to § 2(1) WissZeitVG until December, 31, 2029Research Associate (PhD position) for the DFG project (65%)Working the Plantationocene. Ecological Labour Regimes of the Palm Oil Value Chain (PALMWORK)PALMWORK examines the relationship between labour and the environment along the palm oil value chain, particularly in the areas of production (plantations and oil mills) and social reproduction. The project is designed as a qualitative comparative analysis of case studies from Northeast India, Ghana and Colombia. It builds on re-search from the fields of labour regime analysis, (feminist) labour geography, environmental labour studies and political ecology on the materiality of nature and the society–nature metabolism. The project is being carried out as part of the DFG Priority Programme 2575 'Sustainability and Resilience of Agri-Food Chains' and consists of three sub-projects located at the University of Bonn, the Free University of Berlin and the University of Kassel. The position is for the sub-project in Northeast India, and is based at Bonn University.Tasks:- Field research with plantation and mill workers in North-East India- Contribution to joint publications- Contribution to science communicationProfile:- A completed academic degree (Master's) in the social sciences or earth sci-ences (political science, human geography, regional studies, sociology or equivalent)- Willingness to conduct independent field research in Northeast India- Very good spoken and written English- Good communication and teamwork skills- Intercultural and diversity competenceDesirable:- Experience of conducting independent research in India- Good knowledge of qualitative research methods- Experience with working and researching with (palm oil) workers- Good command of a language spoken in Northeast India (e.g. Assamese, Bengali, Nepali)- Good knowledge of the project's research area (political ecology, political economy, analysis of labour regimes, environmental labour studies, labour ge ography)What we offer:- Opportunity to pursue a PhD- Be part of a cutting-edge research team- Be part of a larger network of scholars in the DFG Special Programme- Flexible working hours and the ability to work from home- Remuneration in accordance with TV-L pay grade 13The University of Bonn promotes an open, respectful, and non-discriminatory academic culture and is actively committed to equal opportunity and family friendliness. We aim to eliminate structural disadvantages and to strengthen diversity in research, teaching, and administration. Therefore, we welcome all applications, regard-less of ethnic or social background, gender, sexual orientation, religion or belief, disability, or age.Applications from women and people with a documented severe disability (or equivalent status) will be given preferential consideration in accordance with the State Equality Act (LGG) NRW and Social Code (SGB) IXProject start is January 1st, 2027. Please send your application (with motivation letter, CV and writing sample (if available) with the application code 2026/447 to opye@uni-bonn.de. Application deadline is 22th November, 2026.
